title: Horizon Call of the Mountain
subtitle: Horizon seen from the next handhold
summary: Horizon Call of the Mountain is Guerrilla and Firesprite's virtual-reality adventure, released with PlayStation VR2 on 22 February 2023.
body: Horizon Call of the Mountain is Guerrilla and Firesprite's virtual-reality adventure, released with PlayStation VR2 on 22 February 2023. Ryas, a former Shadow Carja soldier seeking a pardon, investigates a disturbance among the machines. The first-person viewpoint brings the scale of Horizon's world close to the player, from a cliff directly above to a mechanical creature moving nearby. Climbing supplies much of the journey, making the next handhold and the height beneath it practical parts of moving through the landscape.

The motion controllers let the player reach for grips, ropes and vines, supporting progress through physical gestures. Later tools include pickaxes and a grappling hook, extending the kinds of surface and gap that can be crossed. Different movement options accommodate how players prefer to navigate in virtual reality. The environment is read through reach and distance: a visible destination becomes a series of manageable holds, while looking away from the wall reveals the height gained during the ascent and the route still to travel.

Ryas's investigation gives the climbs and encounters a place within the wider Horizon setting. The game was developed alongside Forbidden West but built in Unreal Engine 4, with VR2 features such as eye tracking and haptic feedback informing its presentation. Alistair Kerley and Frankie Harper composed the score. Its narrower, first-person journey offers another relationship with a familiar world: terrain becomes something the player grips and traverses, and the machines are encountered at the bodily scale suggested by standing beneath them.
